Yes, the corpus indicates that contacting third parties such as relatives, friends or referees is restricted, and doing so in an intrusive or humiliating way counts as prohibited harassment.

- **General recovery conduct (Para 100, RBI NBFC Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025):** NBFCs and their agents must not use intimidation or harassment in debt collection, including acts meant to humiliate publicly or intrude on the privacy of the debtor's family members, referees and friends. Also prohibited are persistent calls to the borrower, calls before 8:00 a.m. or after 7:00 p.m., threatening or anonymous calls, inappropriate messages, and false or misleading representations. These directions do not apply to microfinance loans.
- **Microfinance loans (Para 91):** Harsh recovery methods are deemed to include harassing relatives, friends or co-workers of the borrower, and persistent calls before 9:00 a.m. or after 6:00 p.m.
- **Recovery agents (Para 98):** NBFCs must train agents on hours of calling and privacy of customer information.

The corpus does not expressly say whether a one-off, neutral contact with a listed third party (for example, to get a message to the borrower) is permitted, nor does it separately address guarantors or co-obligors. I did not search for those points, so I can't confirm the position on them from these sources.

content.text: The RBI NBFC Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 govern recovery agents: NBFCs must obtain agents' undertaking to follow the code of conduct, agents must follow the Fair Practices Code and the NBFC's own collection code, and they must keep customer information confidential (paras 98–99). Recovery must not involve undue harassment, such as persistent calls at odd hours or muscle power, and staff must be trained to treat borrowers appropriately (para 20). For microfinance loans, harsh methods are prohibited and listed examples include abusive language and persistent or untimely calls (para 91). NBFCs must run due diligence on recovery agents, including antecedent verification (para 94), and must maintain a dedicated mechanism for recovery grievances, with its details given to the borrower at loan disbursal (para 92). I did not find a separate provision requiring borrower-facing disclosure of recovery practices, so that part of the question is only partly covered; the Board-approved policies and Fair Practices Code requirements (paras 7 and A.1) are the closest related rules.

findings.obligation: The NBFC must ensure that it and its agents do not intimidate or harass anyone in debt collection. This includes acts that intrude on the privacy of the debtor's family members, referees and friends, and sending inappropriate messages on mobile or social media. The corpus does not contain any provision that specifically addresses collecting or using a borrower's contact list or third-party data for recovery, so the answer has to be pieced together from the general rules.

- **DPDP Rule 3 (notice):** Any notice to a Data Principal must be understandable on its own, and must give clear, plain-language details sufficient for specific and informed consent, including an itemised description of the personal data and the specified purpose with a description of the goods, services or uses. It must also give a link to the app or website and the means to withdraw consent (as easy as giving it), exercise rights, and complain to the Board.
- **Third-party contacts:** The corpus has no DPDP rule that separately addresses non-borrower contacts, so I could not confirm whether those people must receive their own notice or consent. On the face of Rule 3, the notice and consent obligation attaches to the Data Principal, and a contact is a Data Principal in their own right, but the corpus does not say how that applies to a borrower's phone book.
- **RBI digital lending (Credit Facilities Directions, para 13):** Any data collection by the NBFC's digital lending apps and those of its lending service providers must be need-based, with the borrower's prior and explicit consent and an audit trail. Sharing with third parties is also governed by this paragraph, though the retrieved excerpt was cut off before its full terms.
- **RBI recovery conduct (Responsible Business Conduct Directions, para 100):** The NBFC must ensure that it and its agents do not intimidate or harass anyone in debt collection, including acts meant to humiliate publicly or intrude on the privacy of the debtor's family members. This bars using contacts to pressure third parties.
- **Recovery agents (paras 95–96 and Credit Facilities para 9(6)):** Recovery agents must be notified to the borrower with their authorisation details and the NBFC's and agency's contact details.

Taken together, collecting a contact list would need the borrower's explicit consent under the RBI digital lending rule and a DPDP-compliant notice. Using those contacts to chase recovery would fall within the RBI prohibition on privacy intrusion and harassment. Whether the contacts themselves need separate notice is an open point that should be checked against the full DPDP Act and the RBI text.

61. Secrecy Obligations and Sharing of Information:
(1) The NBFC shall maintain secrecy regarding the customer information that
arises out of the contractual relationship between the NBFC and the customer.
(2) The NBFC shall treat information collected from customers for the purpose of
opening of account as confidential and shall not divulge details thereof for the purpose
of cross-selling, or for any other purpose without the express permission of the
customer.
(3) While considering the requests for data / information from Government and
other agencies, the NBFC shall satisfy itself that the information being sought is not
of such a nature as will violate the provisions of the laws relating to secrecy in the
transactions.
(4) The exceptions to the said rule shall be as under:
(i) Where disclosure is under compulsion of law,
(ii) Where there is a duty to the public to disclose,
(iii) Where the interest of the NBFC requires disclosure, and
(iv) Where the disclosure is made with the express or implied consent of the
customer.

13. Collection, usage and sharing of data with third parties
(1) An NBFC shall ensure that any collection of data by their DLA and DLA of their
LSP is need-based and with prior and explicit consent of the borrower having
audit trail. In any case, an NBFC shall also ensure that DLA of NBFC / LSP
desist from accessing mobile phone resources like file and media, contact list,
call logs, telephony functions, etc. A one-time access can be taken for camera,
microphone, location or any other facility necessary for the purpose of on-
boarding / KYC requirements only, with the explicit consent of the borrower.
(2) The borrower shall be provided with an option to give or deny consent for use
of specific data, restrict disclosure to third parties, data retention, revoke
consent already granted to collect personal data and if required, make the
NBFC / LSP delete / forget the data.
(3) The purpose of obtaining borrowers’ consent needs to be disclosed at each
stage of interface with the borrowers.
(4) Explicit consent of the borrower shall be taken before sharing personal
information with any third party, except for cases where such sharing is
required as per statutory or regulatory requirement.
